title: Acyclic pro-etale hypercover model for a bounded-below module complex
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with small pro-etale site and universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on that site, $W$ a site object, and $U_\bullet\to W$ a hypercover whose terms are weakly contractible, with these notions as in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-affine-acyclic-hypercover]. Let $E^\bullet$ be a complex of sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with $E^q=0$ for $q<N$, for some integer $N$. Define the total complex of $B^{p,q}=E^q(U_p)$, $p\geq0$, by $\operatorname{Tot}(B)^r=\bigoplus_{p+q=r,\,p\geq0}E^q(U_p)$ and differential $\delta+(-1)^p d_E$ on $B^{p,q}$, where $\delta=\sum_{j=0}^{p+1}(-1)^j d_j^*$ is the alternating face restriction. Each displayed sum is finite because $N\leq q\leq r$. Then there is an isomorphism in $D(R(W)\text{-}\operatorname{Mod})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], natural in $E^\bullet$, $$\operatorname{Tot}(B)\simeq R\Gamma(W,QE^\bullet).$$ Here $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms and $R\Gamma(W,-)$ means derived evaluation: replace $E^\bullet$ by a bounded-below complex $J^\bullet$ of injective module sheaves and a quasi-isomorphism $E^\bullet\to J^\bullet$, and take $J^\bullet(W)$. Existence of such chain-level resolutions and their K-injectivity are as in [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution]. In particular every quasi-isomorphism of bounded-below complexes induces a quasi-isomorphism of these total complexes.

proof.text: Put $A=R(W)$ and write $T(E)=\operatorname{Tot}(E^q(U_p))$. Regard each section module as an $A$-module via $U_p\to W$. Semilinearity of restriction gives $A$-linearity of the face maps, since all faces are over $W$. The simplicial identities pair the terms of $\delta^2$ with opposite signs; naturality of $d_E$ gives $\delta d_E=d_E\delta$. Thus $(\delta+(-1)^p d_E)^2=0$: the mixed terms have coefficients $(-1)^p$ and $(-1)^{p+1}$. There are at most $r-N+1$ nonzero summands in total degree $r$, and none when $r<N$. Coefficient chain maps act on each summand and commute with both differentials. This defines the additive total functor $T$ and its chain maps.

source.place: Tag 09A2, label lemma-compute-cohomology; explicit total signs

proof.text: Evaluation at each $U_p$ is exact on module sheaves. Indeed the kernel and cokernel descriptions for module sheaves identify them after forgetting coefficients with those for abelian sheaves. A module epimorphism therefore induces an abelian-sheaf epimorphism, which is locally surjective by the abelian-sheaf epimorphism criterion. The set-sheaf epimorphism criterion turns the same local lifts into an epimorphism of underlying set sheaves. Weak contractibility then makes evaluation of this map surjective at $U_p$. Evaluation preserves kernels because these are computed sectionwise. Consequently it preserves short exact sequences, cycles, boundaries and cohomology. In particular a quasi-isomorphism $E\to F$ induces a quasi-isomorphism $E(U_p)\to F(U_p)$ for every $p$. This argument uses the definition of weak contractibility, not the existence or affineness clause of the hypercover node.

source.place: Tag 0946, label lemma-w-contractible, part (1), with module kernels/cokernels Tag 03DA and epimorphism criteria Tags 03CN, 00WN

proof.text: Apply the general small-ringed-site bounded-below resolution theorem to choose a chain quasi-isomorphism $i:E\to J$, with $J$ bounded below, termwise injective and K-injective. Its smallness hypothesis is exactly the chosen site/universe convention. This theorem supplies a chain map, whereas an abstract isomorphism of objects of $D^+$ alone would not. Choose a common lower bound $M$ for $E$ and $J$. For the double complexes below reindex the coefficient coordinate by $t=q-M\geq0$, retaining the original differential, so total degree $n=p+t$ corresponds to original degree $n+M$. This is relabelling the complexes, not application of a signed derived shift.

source.place: Tag 09A2, second proof paragraph; derived.tex Tag 013K, label lemma-injective-resolutions-exist, part (3)

proof.text: Set $B_E^{p,t}=E^{t+M}(U_p)$ and $B_J^{p,t}=J^{t+M}(U_p)$. The bicomplex map induced by $i$ is a quasi-isomorphism in each vertical complex at fixed $p$, by step 2. Apply the first-quadrant total comparison to the transposed bicomplexes, whose resolution columns at fixed $p$ are these vertical complexes. The signed interchange $x\mapsto(-1)^{pt}x$ identifies their total complexes with the original ones: changing $p$ to $p+1$ changes this sign by $(-1)^t$, and changing $t$ to $t+1$ changes it by $(-1)^p$, precisely the factors interchanging $d_1+(-1)^p d_2$ and $d_2+(-1)^t d_1$. It also commutes with the map induced by $i$. Undo the degree relabelling. Hence $\beta=T(i):T(E)\to T(J)$ is a quasi-isomorphism of $A$-module complexes.

source.place: Tag 09A2, second proof paragraph; homology.tex Tag 0132, label lemma-first-quadrant-ss, first filtration

proof.text: For each $q$, apply the ringed-hypercover injective augmentation theorem to $I=J^q$. The small pro-etale site has representable sheaves as in the cited hypercover notion, and $U_\bullet\to W$ is the given all-degree hypercover. The theorem gives the canonical row quasi-isomorphism $J^q(W)[0]\to(J^q(U_p),\delta)_{p\geq0}$ in $A$-modules. It requires module injectivity only; no assertion that the underlying abelian sheaf of $J^q$ is injective is made. This yields $H^0=J^q(W)$ through restriction and $H^p=0$ for $p>0$.

source.place: Tags 01GE and 01GW, labels lemma-acyclic-hypercover-sheaves and lemma-injective-trivial-cech; module-coefficient Hom argument

proof.text: Form the first-quadrant bicomplex $S$ with $S^{0,t}=J^{t+M}(W)$ and $S^{p,t}=0$ for $p>0$, with vertical differential $d_J$. Restriction into $U_0$ gives a bicomplex map $S\to B_J$: the two restrictions to $U_1$ agree because both structural maps compose to $U_1\to W$, so $\delta^0$ kills the augmentation; it also commutes with $d_J$. At each fixed $t$ its horizontal complex map is the row quasi-isomorphism of step 5. These are exactly the $\mathrm{flip}.X\,t$ complexes in the cited comparison theorem. Thus its total map is a quasi-isomorphism. Since $\operatorname{Tot}(S)=J(W)$ after the degree relabelling, this is the restriction augmentation $\alpha:J(W)\to T(J)$, supported in $p=0$. In $D(A\text{-}\operatorname{Mod})$ both $Q\alpha$ and $Q\beta$ are invertible, so $c_E=(Q\alpha)^{-1}\circ Q\beta:T(E)\xrightarrow{\sim}J(W)=R\Gamma(W,QE)$ is the asserted isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09A2, final proof paragraph; homology.tex Tag 0132, second filtration

proof.text: Check independence and naturality on morphisms rather than merely on cohomology groups. For a coefficient chain map $f:E\to F$ and resolutions $i_E:E\to J_E$, $i_F:F\to J_F$, the localization-Hom bijection into the K-injective target $J_F$ represents $(Qi_F)(Qf)(Qi_E)^{-1}$ by a chain map $a:J_E\to J_F$, unique up to homotopy. Injectivity of that bijection says $a i_E$ and $i_F f$ are homotopic. If $h$ is such a coefficient homotopy, its total homotopy on $E^q(U_p)$ is $H=(-1)^p h(U_p)$. In $d_T H+H d_T$ the horizontal terms cancel, since restriction commutes with $h$ and the signs are $(-1)^p$ and $(-1)^{p+1}$; the vertical terms are $d h+h d$. Hence $T(a)\beta_E$ and $\beta_F T(f)$ agree after localization. Evaluation carries $h$ to $h(W)$, so it also respects homotopies. The augmentation is strictly natural: $T(a)\alpha_E=\alpha_F a(W)$, since both components are restriction composed with $a$. Inverting the two augmentations gives $Qa(W)c_E=c_F QT(f)$. Here $Qa(W)$ is the resolution representative of $R\Gamma(W,Qf)$. Taking $f=1_E$ with two choices of resolution proves independence of $c_E$ and of the morphism representative; applying the same bijection to composites and identities proves functoriality. No functorial choice of injective resolutions is needed.

source.place: Tag 070I, label lemma-K-injective; Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/DerivedCategory/KInjective.lean, Qh_map_bijective, lines 41-46; explicit total homotopy sign calculation

proof.text: Finally let $f:E\to F$ be any quasi-isomorphism between bounded-below coefficient complexes. Choose a common lower bound for both complexes, allowing their originally given bounds to differ. Step 2 makes every vertical section-complex map a quasi-isomorphism. Repeat the transposition and finite-diagonal comparison of step 4 directly on $f$ to obtain that $T(f)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus the last assertion follows at chain level and does not require a converse claim about arbitrary isomorphisms in a derived category.
